evidence: H-02: Buoy3Pool.safetyCheck only checks a/b and a/c ratios within BASIS_POINTS; by transitivity b/c is only within 2*BASIS_POINTS, so the precision check is imprecise and b/c must be checked as well.

M-04: switchEoaOnly() lets the owner disable preventSmartContracts, allowing any smart contract to interact and exploit underlying flash loan vulnerabilities; the SC-protection (flashloan mitigation) can be turned off/bypassed.

H-02: The NatSpec states safetyCheck verifies Curve and an external oracle, but no external oracle calls are checked (both _ratio and lastRatio come from Curve), and inverted ratios a/b vs b/a are not symmetric, so the oracle safety validation is incomplete/incorrect.

M-03: GovDev.sol's updateSolution upgrades the contract via the Diamond construction; 'any functionality can be changed and all the funds can be accessed/rugged' - an unrestricted owner-controlled upgrade path (centralization/reputation risk).

executeTrades checks finalOutputAmount >= finalAmountMin BEFORE sending funds; for a fee-on-transfer toToken the transfer reduces the amount, so the user may receive less than finalAmountMin -- the minimum-out/slippage check is premature and defeated by the fee.

M-03: name/symbol can be set back to empty strings, 'uninitializing the contract and letting the initialize(..) function be called again... In general, it shouldn't be possible to initialize more than once.' Owner may hide minting additional tokens, or anyone can take control and mint any number of tokens.

H-01: A malicious early user can lock() with only 1 wei of XDEFI and make _pointsPerUnit very large via updateDistribution() (callable by anyone), causing future users not to be able to lock()/unlock() due to overflow in arithmetic related to _pointsMultiplier; the contract malfunctions and freezes users' funds. Fix adds a minimum units locked / initial totalUnits offset (lower-bound).

M-01: _generateNewTokenId() uses totalSupply()+1 in the lower 128 bits; because unlocked positions are deleted and NFTs are burned via merge(), _generateNewTokenId() may reuse the same totalSupply() value, causing _safeMint() to fail (duplicate tokenId) when the same amount_ and duration_ are used.

M-01: In CrossAnchorBridge, all `require` that 'Check that token is a whitelisted token' is commented out (e.g. `// require(whitelistedStableTokens[token]);`). Users can send non-whitelisted tokens that cannot be processed on the Terra side, freezing funds on the bridge.

M-05: When bufferCap is updated in _updateAddress, the address's allowed buffer (bufferStored) is replenished to the entire bufferCap; an address can frontrun updateAddress, spend its entire buffer, then have it replenished and spend it again. Recommended fix keeps old buffer capped by new bufferCap (min(_bufferCap, newBuffer)). The core defect is incorrect buffer accounting/state restored on cap update.

M-02: RateLimited.setBufferCap first updates the buffer (_updateBufferStored) and then sets the new cap, but does not apply the new cap to the updated buffer, so the buffer value can be larger than the new bufferCap and actions consuming more than the new cap can be performed. Buffer state is left inconsistent with the new cap.

M-01: storedTotalAssets is a cached value that only includes unlockedRewards when the cycle ends, so 'storedTotalAssets -= amount' reverts (underflow) when the withdrawal amount exceeds it, blocking users from withdrawing until rewardsCycleEnd.

M-05: FlywheelCore.setFlywheelRewards doesn't check that newFlywheelRewards' FlywheelCore is this contract; if it isn't, users irrevocably lose access to reward funds. Fix is to require address(newFlywheelRewards.flywheel) == this.

M-04: 'Protocol doesn't handle fee on transfer tokens'. Since _tokenContract can be any token, fee-on-transfer tokens cause the contract's recorded amount (_amount) to exceed the actual received balance; PoC shows with a 5% fee the contract ends with less than tracked, so 'other user's funds might be drained.' This is a fee-on-transfer accounting mismatch.

M-01 'Possible lost msg.value': in depositCollateral, if asset is ERC20 but value is sent, or if asset is ETH and msg.value > _amount, the excess/value is lost; no check that msg.value == 0 (ERC20) or msg.value == _amount (ETH).
M-02: In YieldManager, UNISWAP_FEE is hardcoded, so all ETH-path swaps use the wrong (1%) pool instead of optimal 0.3%/0.1% pools, creating significant loss of revenue.

M-07: residual ERC20 allowance after _mintFCashPosition (_maxSendAmount not fully consumed). If the upgradeable Notional fCash wrapper is compromised, it can pull funds from the SetToken via the residual allowance; 'a lazy manager might set _maxAssetAmount to type(uint256).max', exposing SetToken assets to theft.

M-01: attacker sends fCash of wrong maturity/asset to the create2 address before deployment (onERC1155Received not yet active). Afterwards the wrapper holds >1 asset, so onERC1155Received reverts and 'minting becomes impossible' — availability loss / DoS, not theft.

H-01: previewWithdraw/previewMint call convertToShares which rounds down, but EIP-4626 requires rounding up for these methods, so the vault is shortchanged and composability/integration breaks. Judge raised to High specifically as an EIP-4626 conformance/rounding issue.

M-08: wfCash is an ERC777 token; the tokensToSend (_callTokensToSend) hook hands control to the attacker mid-issuance, enabling cross-contract reentrancy (call CompoundLeverageModule.sync + manager.removeModule) that corrupts position accounting and DoSes/bricks the SetToken.

M-03: _isUnderlying() checks _paymentToken == underlyingToken first, but for NonMintable fCash the asset token IS the underlying, so it wrongly returns true. This makes mint/redeem call NotionalV2 with useUnderlying==true, which reverts; mintFCashPosition()/redeemFCashPosition() become unusable (revert/DoS) for those tokens.

M-01: launching a project with two identical locked splits, then updating to only one drops a locked split that should remain, because 'the check of the locked split is not suitable for duplicated cases.' Fix: prevent duplicates or track matches.

M-12: When the owner calls changeTokenOf, the project's token is changed, making oldToken holders unable to redeem overflowing assets; mitigation suggests adding a delay or a conversion function. Owner-privileged action strands holders.

M-04: A project owner can set ~389+ splits (min percent of 1), so a user calling distributeReservedTokensOf hits the block gas limit and loses gas without receiving their split. Judge: 'similar to the unbounded loop and other out-of-gas issues.'

permit() check 'if (recoveredAddress != address(0) && recoveredAddress != owner)' lets recoveredAddress==0x0 pass; anyone can permit themselves as spender for the zero address and drain the protocol by transferring burned tokens back to themselves.
Docs say withdraw 'amount' = underlying assets, but Yearn's withdraw 'amount' = shares burnt; this either reverts (cannot redeem zcTokens) or permanently locks excess funds in the vault.
Compounding.underlying() calls IYearnVault(c).underlying(), a property that does not exist in Yearn vaults, so the call always reverts, making it impossible to create a MarketPlace for a Yearn vault.

If maturityRate is still 0 after maturity deadline, previewWithdraw multiplication by maturityRate returns 0 so ZcToken.withdraw sends 0 underlying tokens to the user; view functions use the stale/uninitialized saved maturityRate.

MarketPlace.authRedeem() calls ISwivel.authRedeem() but Swivel only has authRedeemZcToken(); the non-existent interface method causes MarketPlace.authRedeem() and thus ZcToken.withdraw() to fail forever.

H-02: In Witch.sol::_calcAuction, when line.proportion is small and art falls below debt.min, the code sets art = balances.art and consequently ink = balances.ink, so the WHOLE collateral and debt go to auction even though only a fraction was meant for auction. Judge: 'users may lose their entire collateral when only part of their collateral should have been put to auction.'

Leftover shares in liquidateClean are only subtracted from pair totals, but not from user's borrowed shares; borrower's shares stay >0 while still insolvent, so it can be liquidated again and 'messes up the whole pair accounting, with total asset amounts reducing and total borrow amounts and shares reducing' until totals underflow and the pool locks.

When _addInterest() is called post maturity, the penalty rate is applied since the last time it was called, including the pre-maturity period; the rate-selection logic fails to split the interval so borrowers are charged higher (penalty) interest for time before maturity, producing excessive/incorrect interest accrual.

M-05: 'repay function can be frontrun by an attacker. Say an attacker pay a small amount of debt for the victim... when the victim's transaction gets executed, the require condition will fail... Hence an attacker can DOS the repay function for the victim user.' The strict require(debt >= amount) lets a front-runner shrink the debt and force the victim's repay to revert.

M-18: 'Chainlink's multisigs can immediately block access to price feeds at will. When this occurs, executing feeds[token].feed.latestAnswer() will revert so calling viewPrice and getPrice also revert, which cause denial of service' on borrow/withdraw/force-replenish/liquidate. The feed return is not safely handled / no fallback, making the protocol DoS-able via Chainlink dependency.

M-16: 'when the forceReplenish function is not called... the user can just call the repay function to repay the original debt and the withdraw function to receive all of the deposited collateral even when the user has a DBR deficit already... the Market contract would receive less DOLA.' The user circumvents the intended replenishment charging mechanism.

There is no limits on _updateDAORevenueCommission() except not exceeding MODULO, which means it can be set to a 100%; no maximum cap on how much commission DAO can take, so node runners can receive 0 rewards.

_distributeETHRewardsToUserForToken has require(_recipient != address(0)); since _burn passes to=address(0), any withdraw burning GiantLP reverts on the zero-address check and users' funds are stuck in the Giant Pool.

bringUnusedETHBackIntoGiantPool() brings unused ETH back to the giant pool but does not increase idleETH, so the contract loses tracking of real idle ETH and the returned ETH cannot be reused for withdrawing/staking.
During rotating LPTokens it is not checked that the _newLPToken is related to a banned BLS public key; recommended fix adds require(isBLSPublicKeyBanned(...) == false) to rotateLPTokens.
GiantPoolBase.withdrawETH requires amount >= MIN_STAKING_AMOUNT; this check serves no purpose and can leave a user with sub-MIN_STAKING_AMOUNT dust that cannot be withdrawn.
registerBLSPublicKeys uses isBLSPublicKeyPartOfLSDNetwork (only checks membership) instead of isBLSPublicKeyBanned, so banned BLS public keys can still be registered successfully.
batchRotateLPTokens requires GiantLP balance >= 0.5 ether; this hardcoded threshold does not scale and can make the function impossible to call; should be dynamically calculated from total supply.
dETH / ETH / LPTokenETH can become depegged due to ETH 2.0 reward slashing; on a slashing penalty the ETH will not be pegged and the validator cannot maintain the 32 ETH balance.

withdrawETHForStaking does not verify _smartWallet is a valid existent wallet; a non-zero non-existent address passes and the ETH transfer 'will always return true', permanently locking the ETH. The report itself recommends adding a validity (owner) check before transfer.

executeAsSmartWallet is payable but does not forward the sent ETH to the smart wallet; 'the sent ETH amount is locked in the LiquidStakingManager contract' while the same amount is deducted from the smart wallet balance.

updateAccumulatedETHPerLP() is only called when the first BLS key is part of the syndicate, so '_distribute would use stale value, and users will not receive as many rewards as they should' — flawed i==0 gating of the reward accumulator update.
deployLPToken has 'no chain.id in the data'; an attacker can replay the action on the correct chain and 'steal the funds a-la the wintermute gnosis safe attack' by creating the same address.

The 0.5 ether lpTokenETH balance check is insufficient because users can deposit then burn to game it, so 'malicious users can keep bouncing LP tokens around and prevent them from being available for actual staking' — griefing that prevents holdings from being staked.

Because of the i==0 condition, 'if the first BLS public key is not part of the syndicate, then _claimFundsFromSyndicateForDistribution will not be called, even on BLS keys that are eligible for syndicate rewards,' leading to reduced rewards.

subtag: Invalid Slippage Control / Missing slippage check
evidence: H-02: 'While the minLpTokenAmount protects from slippage when adding liquidity, it doesn't protect from providing liquidity at different K' - the excess of disproportionate tokens gets donated to the pool, so LPs lose funds. Sponsor fix added min/max price bounds, confirming the existing slippage control is insufficient.

H-03: 'First depositor can break minting of shares... users may not receive shares in exchange for their deposits if the total asset amount has been manipulated through a large donation.' Attacker mints 1 wei LP, donates 1e9 tokens, normal users then receive 0 LP due to rounding - the classic first-depositor inflation attack, matching the taxonomy convention example (gALCX) labeled Input Validation / Inflation Attack.

subtag: Violating CEI / Missing nonReentrant, ERC777 Callback
evidence: H-04: claimRewards in MultiRewardStaking does not follow checks-effects-interactions; accruedRewards is cleared AFTER the transfer instead of before. ERC777 tokens let the attacker register a tokensReceived hook to reenter claimRewards in the for-loop and drain the entire reward balance.

H-01: 'In the spec, the pre-defined limit of ETH is 0.01 ETHs. But the actual limit in the code is 1*10e17 which is 0.1 ETH.' Judge: 'limit is 10x higher than it should be... funds can be lost if pools are manipulated.' The hardcoded MaxSwapAmount param contradicts the documented spec value.

claimPrizesForRound iterates up to the current global maxPrizeCount; when the owner decreases maxPrizeCount after a round's prizes were set, winners with higher prize indices can never claim, and clearing the user's entries on claim means reverting the value doesn't restore claimability — the per-round prize state is inconsistent with the mutable global count.

H-03: erc721DecreaseIsolateSupplyOnLiquidate() never clears tokenData.lockerAddr, so after liquidation validateWithdrawERC721 reverts on the lockerAddr==address(0) check and the user is 'Unable to retrieve NFT' — the NFT is permanently locked due to the missing state reset.

M-09: After a full isolateRedeem (scaledAmount->0) the loanStatus stays ACTIVE and erc721TokenData.LockerAddr is not set to address(0), so the user cannot withdraw the NFT and is 'forced to borrow again in order to unlock their NFTs'.

H-05: 'Bad debt is never handled' — ERC20 positions only partially liquidate and ERC721 positions are unprofitable to liquidate, so leftover debt is never repaid and 'the protocol will not have enough liquidity to fulfill withdrawals, DoSing them forever'.

M-07: executeYieldBorrowERC20() computes totalSupply with erc20GetTotalCrossSupply(assetData, groupData.borrowIndex) — the wrong index; it should use assetData.supplyIndex, making the yieldCap check inaccurate.

M-15: When botAdmin force-unstakes, the staker pays unstakeFine but only nftDebt is sent to the pool; the unstakeFine stays in the contract and 'there are no functions that send the collected funds to the admin, and so they will remain in the contract forever'.

M-17: Auction end is computed as bidStartTimestamp + nftAssetData.auctionDuration; because auctionDuration is mutable via setAssetAuctionParams, changing it retroactively shortens/extends already-running auctions, catching participants off guard.

M-20: unwrapNativeTokenInWallet is called with msgSender instead of receiver, so the protocol tries to pull wrapped tokens from msg.sender (who may not hold them) instead of the receiver, causing withdraw/borrow to fail when msg.sender != receiver.

M-08: erc20TransferInBidAmount and similar functions enforce require(poolSizeAfter == poolSizeBefore + amount), which always reverts for fee-on-transfer tokens even though the README states fee-on-transfer ERC20s are in scope.

M-06: 'if (nextDuration.raw() > MAX_CLOCK_DURATION.raw() - CLOCK_EXTENSION.raw()) condition check is vulnerable.' At SPLIT_DEPTH-1 the boundary case bypasses the double extension, so 'a team's clock may run out prematurely', denying the ability to generate the trace and counterclaim.

M-05: PANIC state 'can always be attacked', so 'none of the claims at SPLIT_DEPTH are challenged' because SPLIT_DEPTH is even; fix is 'Set the split_depth to an odd number.' Assessed type: DoS. Claims become unchallengeable -> output root unrecoverable.

H-01: 'DISPUTED_L2_BLOCK_NUMBER passed to the VM is always starting block + trace index + 1' uncapped; fix 'min(..., l2BlockNumber())'. Wrong block number is passed so valid claims earlier than safe head can be challenged -> incorrect game resolution, not Out of Gas.
